studio/three-passes-through-an-image.htm.title: Three passes through an image
studio/three-passes-through-an-image.htm.description:
Home · Choose a comparisonChoose one reference. Record its maker or community, place, medium, and source link. Draw the largest three shapes, then mark the spaces between them. Write one thing you can see without assigning a symbolic meaning.Open one of its linked comparison pages. Draw both references at the same size. Compare a single feature: line thickness, spacing, contour, repetition, or material construction. Note one difference as carefully as one resemblance.Choose your own subject. Make three variations by changing only one variable, such as spacing or proportion. Label the source study and your invention separately. Record which operation you borrowed and what you changed.
Save the result in My studies, with links back to the references. Return to the original source before interpreting an inscription, cultural motif, or artist’s intention.

studio/using-savl.html.title: Using SAVL
studio/using-savl.html.description:
Open the visual atlas to scan images, or choose a theme from SAVL - Start here. Each image has a linked reference note. All downloaded photographs keep the source file’s proportions; some sources include borders or installation surroundings.Use Obsidian search for words such as spirals, stepped, silhouette, gold, or a maker’s name. Reference properties record maker, place, date, medium, themes, motifs and source. The favorite checkbox lets you mark references worth returning to.
Duplicate Templates/Reference template, save the full image in Attachments, and record the original page URL. Describe what you can see separately from cultural interpretation. Link at least one theme and two related references. Add the note to the relevant index or theme page; these pages are intentionally editable, not dependent on plugins.Study operations such as spacing, layering, framing and material contrast. Bring your own subject and purpose. Preserve the identities of living artists and communities; a personal experiment should be described as your interpretation. Source access does not by itself grant reproduction rights.The collection is selective; its existing references span ancient objects, Nasca geoglyphs, and modern and contemporary practices in several South American countries. Useful next additions include Southern Cone living textile practices, Guiana and Amazonian makers, Afro-South American practices, architecture and earthworks, each with specific attribution and full images.

info_showOrphanNodes.description: Show nodes that are not connected to any other nodes.

info_showAttachments.description: Show attachments like images and PDFs as nodes in the graph.

info_allowGlobalGraph.description: Allow the user to view the global graph of all nodes.

info_allowExpand.description: Allow the user to pop-out the graph view to take up the whole screen

info_attractionForce.description: How much should linked nodes attract each other? This will make the graph appear more clustered.

info_linkLength.description: How long should the links between nodes be? The shorter the links the more connected nodes will cluster together.

info_repulsionForce.description: How much should nodes repel each other? This will make disconnected parts more spread out.

info_centralForce.description: How much should nodes be attracted to the center? This will make the graph appear more dense and circular.

info_edgePruning.description: Edges with a length above this threshold will not be rendered, however they will still contribute to the simulation. This can help large tangled graphs look more organised. Hovering over a node will still display these links.

info_minNodeRadius.description: How small should the smallest nodes be? The smaller a node is the less it will attract other nodes.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.

info_allowResizing.description: Whether or not to allow the sidebars to be resized

info_allowCollapsing.description: Whether or not to allow the sidebars to be collapsed

info_rightDefaultWidth.description: The default width of the right sidebar

info_leftDefaultWidth.description: The default width of the left sidebar
